nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes and a finite set of states $Q$, and let $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective. For every state $q \in Q$, every symbol $a$ under the input head and every tuple $w$ of symbols under the $k$ work heads (each a bit or blank), the coded action of the code of $M$ under $e$ at state $e(q)$ and symbols $a$, $w$ is the coding, with successor states numbered by $e$,…
nodes.title: The code of a machine takes its coded actions

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes, a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, a symbol $a$ under the input head and symbols $w = (w_i)_{i < k}$ under the work heads (each symbol a bit or the blank), the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ is the coded action of the first table entry of $c$ whose key is $(q, a, w)$, or, if there is no such entry, the halting action, which moves no head, writes and emits nothing, and has no next state.
nodes.title: Action of a code at a key

nodes.summary: Given an input word $x$, a coded action $a$ and an explicit configuration $e$, applying $a$ to $e$ gives the configuration whose state is the next state of $a$; whose input head position is that of $e$, say $p$, moved by the coded input move of $a$, where a left move gives $p - 1$ (truncated at $0$), staying gives $p$, and a right move gives $\min(p + 1, |x| + 1)$; whose work tape $i$ is work tape $i$ of $e$ after…
nodes.title: Applying a coded action

nodes.summary: For a work tape $t$ in zipper form and an integer $j$, the cell of $t$ at $j$ is the symbol at offset $j$ from the head: for $j = n \ge 0$ it is entry $n$ (counting from $0$) of the list of cells from the head rightwards, and for $j = -(n + 1)$ it is entry $n$ of the list of cells left of the head, nearest first; in either case it is the blank when the list has no entry $n$.
nodes.title: Cell of a zipper tape

nodes.summary: A coded action for a machine with $k$ work tapes consists of a coded input-head move; for each of the $k$ work tapes, an optional symbol to write, the symbol being a bit or the blank (so a blank can be written), together with a coded head move; an optional output bit; and an optional next state in $\mathbb{N}$, where no next state means halting. A head move is coded by a natural number: $0$ moves left, $1$ stays,…
nodes.title: Coded actions

nodes.summary: A key of a table entry for a machine with $k$ work tapes is a triple $(q, a, w)$ of a state $q \in \mathbb{N}$, the symbol $a$ under the input head and the symbols $w = (w_i)_{i < k}$ under the $k$ work heads, where each symbol is a bit or the blank.
nodes.title: Keys of a code's table

nodes.summary: A code for a machine with $k$ work tapes over the binary alphabet, with states in $\mathbb{N}$, is a finite list of table entries, each a key (a state together with the symbols under the input head and the $k$ work heads) paired with a coded action. The table is looked up by key, the first matching entry wins, and a missing key halts the machine.
nodes.title: Codes for multi-tape machines

nodes.summary: Let $g : \alpha \to \beta$ be a function, let inputs in $\alpha$ and outputs in $\beta$ be encoded by injective maps into binary words, and let $t, s : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$. Say a machine computes $g$ within $t$ and $s$ when, started on the encoding of any input $x$, it halts with the encoding of $g(x)$ as output, halts within $t(x)$ steps, and visits at most $s(x)$ work-tape cells. Then some binary multi-tape…
nodes.title: Computability over codes

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code with $k$ work tapes, let $g : \alpha \to \beta$ be a function, let inputs in $\alpha$ and outputs in $\beta$ be encoded by injective maps into binary words, and let $t, s : \alpha \to \mathbb{N}$. If the machine of $c$, started on the encoding of any input $x$, halts with the encoding of $g(x)$ as output, halts within $t(x)$ steps, and visits at most $s(x)$ work-tape cells, then some binary…
nodes.title: Computation by a code is finite-state computation

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes and binary words $x$ and $o$, the machine of $c$ computes $o$ on input $x$, that is, it eventually halts on $x$ with output $o$, if and only if there is a clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ such that the clocked evaluator of $c$ run on $x$ for $T$ steps returns $o$.
nodes.title: A code computes exactly what its clocked evaluator returns

nodes.summary: An explicit configuration for a machine with $k$ work tapes consists of an optional state in $\mathbb{N}$ (none when the machine has halted); the input head position, a natural number shifted by one, so that position $0$ is the cell left of the input; the $k$ work tapes, each a zipper (the cells left of the head, nearest first, and the cells from the head rightwards, all further cells blank); and the output written…
nodes.title: Explicit configurations of the code evaluator

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a set of binary words and let $t$ and $s$ map binary words to natural numbers. Say a machine decides $L$ within $t$ and $s$ when, started on any binary word $w$, it halts with the one-bit output $\mathrm{true}$ if $w \in L$ and $\mathrm{false}$ otherwise, halts within $t(w)$ steps, and visits at most $s(w)$ work-tape cells. Then some binary multi-tape machine with finitely many states decides $L$ within…
nodes.title: Decidability over codes

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code with $k$ work tapes, let $L$ be a set of binary words, and let $t$ and $s$ map binary words to natural numbers. If the machine of $c$ decides $L$, that is, started on any binary word $w$ it halts with the one-bit output $\mathrm{true}$ if $w \in L$ and $\mathrm{false}$ otherwise, and if on every binary word $w$ it halts within $t(w)$ steps and visits at most $s(w)$ work-tape cells, then some…
nodes.title: Deciding by a code is finite-state decidability

nodes.summary: For every code $c$ with $k$ work tapes, decoding the natural number $\operatorname{encode}(c)$ returns $c$: $\operatorname{decode}(\operatorname{encode}(c))$ is defined and equals $c$.
nodes.title: Code round-trip

nodes.summary: Decode a head move: `0` moves left, `1` stays, anything else moves right.
nodes.title: Decoding a Turing machine head move

nodes.summary: The code coded by a natural number $n$, if any: decoding under the standard primitive recursive coding of codes, which identifies a code with its table, a list of pairs of a key and a coded action. The result is empty when $n$ codes no code.
nodes.title: Decoding numbers to codes

nodes.summary: Let $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ number the states $Q$ of a binary multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes. The coded action of an action $a$ of the machine under $e$ records as its input-head move the code of the input-head move of $a$ (left $0$, stay $1$, right $2$); for each work tape it records what $a$ writes there and the code of the head move of $a$ there; it records the output bit of $a$, if any; and its next…
nodes.title: Coding an action

nodes.summary: If two codes $c$ and $c'$ with the same number of work tapes have the same numeric code, then $c = c'$.
nodes.title: Injectivity of the numeric coding of codes

nodes.summary: A head move is coded as a natural number: left is $0$, stay is $1$ and right is $2$. Decoding a move code recovers the move.
nodes.title: Coding head moves

nodes.summary: The natural number coding a code $c$: its encoding under the standard primitive recursive coding of codes, which identifies a code with its table, a list of pairs of a key and a coded action.
nodes.title: Numeric coding of codes

nodes.summary: The bijection between explicit configurations and tuples $(q, p, t, o)$ that sends a configuration to its optional state $q$ (empty when halted), its shifted input head position $p \in \mathbb{N}$, its family $t$ of $k$ work tapes (each a zipper) and its output $o$ so far, a list of bits.
nodes.title: Explicit configurations as tuples

nodes.summary: The bijection between coded actions and tuples $(m, w, b, q)$ that sends an action to its coded input head move $m \in \mathbb{N}$, its work tape instructions $w$ (for each of the $k$ work tapes, an optional symbol to write and a coded head move), its optional output bit $b$ and its optional next state $q$.
nodes.title: Coded actions as tuples

nodes.summary: The bijection between codes for machines with $k$ work tapes and finite lists of table entries, each a pair of a key and a coded action, that sends a code to its table.
nodes.title: Multi-tape codes as tables

nodes.summary: For every code $c$, binary input $x$, clock $T \in \mathbb{N}$ and binary word $o$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns $o$ if and only if the machine of $c$, run for $T$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, has halted and its output is $o$.
nodes.title: Evaluator agreement

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ for machines with $k$ work tapes, a binary input $x$, a binary word $o$ and clocks $T \le T'$ in $\mathbb{N}$, if the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ returns $o$ with clock $T$, then it also returns $o$ with clock $T'$.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of the clocked evaluator for multi-tape codes

nodes.summary: The clocked evaluator runs a code $c$ on a binary input $x$ for $T$ steps: it applies the evaluator's step $T$ times to the initial explicit configuration. If the resulting configuration is halted, it returns that configuration's output; otherwise it returns no result.
nodes.title: Clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: A binary machine with finitely many states is simulated, up to an injective state relabelling, by the machine of some code.
nodes.title: Every finite-state machine has a code

nodes.summary: For every finite type $Q$ and every $q_0 \in Q$ there is an injective map $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ with $e(q_0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Numbering a finite type from a chosen element

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $N$ and $q$, this is $q$ as an element of $\{0, \dots, N - 1\}$ if $q < N$, and no value otherwise.
nodes.title: A number as a bounded state

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code with $k$ work tapes and let $N$ be its state bound. For a state $q < N$, a symbol $a$ under the input head and symbols $w$ under the $k$ work heads (each a bit or blank), this is the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ with the same input-head move, work-tape writes and moves, and output, and with its successor state read as a state below $N$; a successor state that is not below $N$ is replaced by halting.
nodes.title: Transition function of a code on bounded states

nodes.summary: The default action of a missing table entry: halt without moving any head, writing any symbol or emitting an output bit.
nodes.title: Halting action

nodes.summary: The initial explicit configuration has state $0$, the input head on the first input cell (position $1$, positions being shifted by one), every work tape blank (both halves of its zipper empty), and empty output.
nodes.title: Initial configuration of the clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: For an input $x$ and a shifted input head position $p$, the input symbol is the blank if $p = 0$; otherwise it is the entry of $x$ at index $p - 1$ (counting from $0$) if $p - 1 < |x|$, and the blank if $p - 1 \ge |x|$.
nodes.title: Input symbol under the input head

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a machine over the binary alphabet with $k$ work tapes, a finite set of states $Q$ and initial state $q_0$, and let $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ be injective with $e(q_0) = 0$. Then the machine of the code of $M$ with states numbered by $e$ simulates $M$ up to the relabelling $e$.
nodes.title: The code of a machine simulates it

nodes.summary: For every code $c$, the machine of $c$ simulates the finite-state machine of $c$ up to the relabelling that sends each state $q < N$, where $N$ is the state bound of $c$, to the natural number $q$.
nodes.title: A code's machine simulates its finite-state machine

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, an input $x$ and a clock $T$, the clocked evaluator of $c$ on $x$ with clock $T$ returns an output if and only if the machine of $c$ runs in time $T$ on $x$, that is, every computation path of that machine on $x$ with at least $T$ steps ends in a halted configuration.
nodes.title: The evaluator returns within the clock exactly when the machine runs in time

nodes.summary: For every $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every language $L$ of binary words, $L \in \mathsf{DSPACE}(s)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $c_1, c_2, k$ and a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes such that the machine of $c$ decides $L$, on every input $w$ runs in space $c_1 s(|w|) + c_2$, and for some $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on every input $w$ runs in time $t(|w|)$.
nodes.title: DSPACE over codes

nodes.summary: For every $t : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and every language $L$ of binary words, $L \in \mathsf{DTIME}(t)$ if and only if there are natural numbers $c_1, c_2, k$ and a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes such that the machine of $c$ decides $L$, on every input $w$ runs in time $c_1 t(|w|) + c_2$, and for some $s : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ on every input $w$ runs in space $s(|w|)$.
nodes.title: DTIME over codes

nodes.summary: For an input of length $n$, a shifted input head position $p$ and a coded move $m$, the new position is $p - 1$ (truncated at $0$) if $m = 0$, $p$ if $m = 1$, and $\min(p + 1, n + 1)$ otherwise, so a move right never passes position $n + 1$, one cell beyond the input.
nodes.title: Input head move of the clocked evaluator

nodes.summary: For a coded move $m$ and a work tape given as a zipper $(l, r)$: if $m = 0$ the head moves one cell left, removing the first cell of $l$ (the blank if $l$ is empty) and putting it in front of $r$; if $m = 1$ the tape is unchanged; otherwise the head moves one cell right, removing the first cell of $r$ (the blank if $r$ is empty) and putting it in front of $l$.
nodes.title: Moving the head of a zipper tape

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a state $q$, an input symbol $a$ and work tape symbols $w$, if the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ has a next state $q'$ (rather than halting), then $q'$ belongs to the set of states of $c$.
nodes.title: Next states of a code lie in its state set

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a machine over the binary alphabet with $k$ work tapes and a finite set of states $Q$, and let $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$. The code of $M$ with states numbered by $e$ has one table entry for each state $q \in Q$, symbol $a$ under the input head and symbols $w$ under the $k$ work heads (each a bit or blank): its key is $(e(q), a, w)$ and its value is the coded action of $M$ in state $q$ reading $a$ and $w$,…
nodes.title: The code of a finite-state binary machine

nodes.summary: The evaluator is primitive recursive in the code, the input and the clock.
nodes.title: The evaluator is primitive recursive

nodes.summary: The symbol read from a work tape given as a zipper $(l, r)$ is the first cell of $r$, or the blank if $r$ is empty.
nodes.title: Symbol under the head of a zipper tape

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, an input $x$ and every $t$, the explicit configuration obtained from the initial one by $t$ steps of the evaluator for $c$ on $x$ represents the configuration that the machine of $c$ reaches after $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$.
nodes.title: The evaluator tracks the machine run

nodes.summary: An explicit configuration $e$ represents a configuration $C$ of CSLib's multi-tape model on input $x$ when they have the same state, the same shifted input head position and the same output, and for every work tape $i$ and every cell $z \in \mathbb{Z}$, the content of cell $z$ of tape $i$ in $C$ equals the cell of tape $i$ of $e$ at offset $z - p_i$ from its head, where $p_i$ is the head position of tape $i$ in $C$.
nodes.title: Explicit configurations representing machine configurations

nodes.summary: The states of a code $c$ are the initial state $0$ and every successor state named in its table. The state bound of $c$ is one more than the largest of them; it is a strict upper bound on the states of $c$.
nodes.title: State bound of a code

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code for a machine with $k$ work tapes. For every binary input $x$ and every number of steps $t$, if the machine of $c$, run for $t$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$, has not halted and is in state $q$, then $q$ lies in the finite set of states of $c$.
nodes.title: Codes denote finite-state machines

nodes.summary: The states of a code $c$ for machines with $k$ work tapes form the finite set of natural numbers consisting of the initial state $0$ and the next state of every table entry of $c$ that does not halt.
nodes.title: States of a multi-tape code

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a code and $x$ a binary input. If an explicit configuration $e$ represents a configuration $C$ of the machine of $c$ on $x$, then the evaluator's step of $e$ for $c$ on $x$ represents the successor of $C$ under the machine of $c$.
nodes.title: The evaluator simulates the machine step for step

nodes.summary: For a code $c$, a binary input $x$ and a configuration $C$ of the machine of $c$ on $x$, the step of the machine of $c$ sends $C$ to its successor under the transition function of $c$: $C$ itself if it has halted, and otherwise the result of applying to $C$ the action that the transition function of $c$ selects for the state of $C$ and the symbols under its heads.
nodes.title: Step of the machine of a code

nodes.summary: One step of the evaluator for a code $c$ on a binary input $x$ leaves an explicit configuration $e$ unchanged if $e$ has halted; if $e$ is in state $q$, it applies to $e$ the coded action of $c$ at $q$, the input symbol at the input head position of $e$ and the symbols under the heads of the work tapes of $e$.
nodes.title: Evaluator step

nodes.summary: A work tape is a pair of finite lists of cells, each cell a bit or blank: the cells left of the head, nearest first, and the cells from the head rightwards; cells beyond both lists are blank.
nodes.title: Work tapes as zippers

nodes.summary: Let $Q$ be a type, $e : Q \to \mathbb{N}$ a map and $a$ an action of a binary machine with $k$ work tapes and states in $Q$. The action that the coded action of $a$, with its successor state numbered by $e$, stands for is $a$ with its successor state relabelled by $e$.
nodes.title: Decoding the coding of an action

nodes.summary: A coded action $a$ stands for the action of CSLib's multi-tape model that moves the input head by the decoded input move of $a$, on each work tape writes the optional symbol that $a$ gives for that tape and moves its head by the decoded move, emits the optional output bit of $a$, and enters the next state of $a$ (halting when there is none).
nodes.title: Decoding a coded action

nodes.summary: For a code $c$ with $k$ work tapes and state bound $N$, this is the binary machine with $k$ work tapes and states $0, 1, \dots, N - 1$ that starts in state $0$ and, in a state $q < N$ reading $a$ under the input head and $w$ under the work heads, takes the action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$, with a successor state not below $N$ replaced by halting. Since every state the machine of $c$ can enter is below $N$, it is the…
nodes.title: The finite-state machine of a code

nodes.summary: The machine of a code $c$ for $k$ work tapes is the machine of CSLib's multi-tape model with $k$ work tapes, the binary alphabet and states in $\mathbb{N}$ whose initial state is $0$ and whose transition function is the transition function of $c$.
nodes.title: The multi-tape machine of a code

nodes.summary: The transition function of a code $c$ sends a state $q$, the symbol $a$ under the input head and the symbols $w$ under the work heads (each a bit or blank) to the action of CSLib's multi-tape model that the coded action of $c$ at $(q, a, w)$ stands for. That coded action is the one of the first table entry of $c$ with key $(q, a, w)$, or, if there is none, the one that halts without moving, writing or emitting.
nodes.title: Transition function of a code

nodes.summary: Writing an optional symbol on a work tape leaves the tape unchanged when no symbol is given; given a symbol $s$ (a bit or blank), it replaces the cell under the head by $s$ and keeps all other cells.
nodes.title: Writing on a zipper tape

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
